acceptance: Under a fixed monotonic clock, deterministic chunking of 1000 narratable paragraphs performs one initial running write, only interval checkpoints at the 200-paragraph policy, and exactly one completed terminal-document write; write count is bounded by ceil(1000/200) plus a small constant rather than approximately 1000.

The 2.0-second checkpoint branch can persist before 200 additional paragraphs, and every persisted running checkpoint has chunks and next_paragraph describing the same processed prefix, including prefixes containing non-narratable separator records.
Cancellation and unexpected failure each persist one terminal cancelled or failed document containing the current consistent chunks/next_paragraph pair before propagating the exception.
Successful completion persists exactly one completed terminal document with next_paragraph set to null and final warnings populated, then returns the report.
Non-terminal progress callbacks are limited by the 0.1-second policy while the terminal completed progress update is always emitted.
Existing deterministic resume, cancellation, separator-prefix, source-fingerprint mismatch, and single-document contract tests remain green.
The AI-assisted chunking implementation and its one-write-per-model-window behavior are unchanged.
The complete pytest and Ruff repository gates pass, with traceability and coverage audits free of blocking findings.
alignment.reason: The defect is localized to one deterministic loop, the intended policies already exist as unused helpers/constants, the persisted schema is unchanged, and focused resume/cancellation contracts bound the risk.
scope: In scope: deterministic chunk_text checkpoint/progress scheduling, focused write-count/progress/resume regression coverage, the existing recoverable-checkpoint requirement, one bounded-performance requirement, the Cleanup/Chunking V2 specification, and Text Chunking component documentation. Out of scope: AI-assisted chunking, checkpoint interval values, chunk semantics, persistence-service atomic-write mechanics, document schema changes, legacy state-layer cleanup tracked by issue #36, and unrelated performance work.
alignment.source: Gitea issue #31: http://192.168.1.15:3001/dpasare/2026_AudioMancer/issues/31; remediation order in issue #40
alignment.understanding: Deterministic chunking currently rewrites and revalidates the growing chunks_text.json document and emits progress after every processed paragraph. Restore the existing 200-paragraph or 2.0-second checkpoint policy and 0.1-second non-terminal progress policy inside chunk_text, while preserving a consistent chunks/next_paragraph resume boundary and mandatory completed, cancelled, and failed terminal persistence. The AI-assisted chunking path and canonical document schema remain unchanged.

intent.statement: Restore bounded checkpoint and progress throttling in deterministic chunking while preserving resume-consistent checkpoints and mandatory terminal persistence

examples: With a fixed clock and 1000 narratable paragraphs, write one initial running document, checkpoints after paragraphs 200, 400, 600, 800, and 1000, then one completed document.
spec_items.statement: REQ-NFR-b22bd156-ca68-45f8-a908-f4678da5464e bounds deterministic running-document checkpoints by processed-paragraph and monotonic-time intervals.
spec_items.threshold: 200 processed paragraphs or 2.0 elapsed monotonic seconds, whichever occurs first

examples: A fixed clock suppresses per-paragraph updates; advancing the clock by 0.1 seconds permits the next non-terminal update, and completion always emits the final total.
spec_items.statement: REQ-NFR-c26cffd5-b20c-4016-9736-7bda8a4f1863 bounds deterministic non-terminal progress callback frequency while retaining terminal completion progress.
spec_items.threshold: 0.1 elapsed monotonic seconds between non-terminal progress emissions

examples: After processing paragraph index k, chunks reflect all narratable records through k and next_paragraph equals k + 2 in the one-based persisted contract, even when record k is a separator.
spec_items.statement: REQ-FUNC-3a22db38-2672-41f2-8e80-e5472c3356a2 requires each persisted running, cancelled, or failed checkpoint to describe one exact processed paragraph prefix.

examples: The sole completed write has next_paragraph set to null and contains final warnings.
spec_items.statement: REQ-FUNC-5afe128a-721a-4e01-b99d-63364cd1fc0e requires one completed terminal persistence before a successful deterministic report returns.

examples: Cancellation after a processed prefix writes status cancelled with that prefix's chunks and next_paragraph, then re-raises.
spec_items.statement: REQ-FUNC-bdc31247-ef93-4a11-8548-d441552b747e requires one cancelled terminal persistence before OperationCancelledError propagates.

examples: A processing exception writes status failed with the current consistent checkpoint, then re-raises the original exception.
spec_items.statement: REQ-FUNC-47c34bc6-1078-4ddd-85d9-98a84de4d6c7 requires one failed terminal persistence before an unexpected processing exception propagates.
